title: Event-Conditioned Diagnostics of Kinematic, Contact, and Object-Permanence Fields in Passive Object-State World Models
abstract: arXiv:2606.28455v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: World models can predict future physical states, but prediction accuracy alone does not explain how physical information is organized and used inside their latent dynamics. We introduce a controlled diagnostic protocol for studying event-conditioned latent physical structure in passive object-state world models. The protocol tests whether hidden representations encode event-regime information, whether event contexts reweight non-exclusive physical field readouts, and whether field-aligned representational components have functional consequences for prediction. Using a balanced controlled-generator dataset with free-motion, collision, and occlusion events, we evaluate recurrent, attention-based, and latent state-space transition models under a fixed-horizon forecasting setup. The models learn useful predictive dynamics and their hidden states support reliable event-regime readout. Event contexts systematically reweight kinematic

translated_title: 事件条件下的被动对象状态世界模型中运动学、接触和对象恒存性场的诊断
translated_abstract: 世界模型能够预测未来的物理状态，但仅凭预测准确性无法解释物理信息在其潜在动态中是如何组织和使用的。我们引入了一种受控诊断协议，用于研究被动对象状态世界模型中事件条件下的潜在物理结构。该协议测试隐藏表示是否编码事件区域信息，事件上下文是否重新加权非排他性的物理场读出，以及场对齐的表示组件是否对预测具有功能性的影响。通过使用包含自由运动、碰撞和遮挡事件的平衡受控生成器数据集，我们在固定时间范围的预测设置下评估了循环、基于注意力以及潜在状态空间转换模型。这些模型学习了有用的预测动态，其隐藏状态支持可靠的事件区域读出。事件上下文系统地重新加权运动学...
tldr: 本文提出了一种受控诊断协议，用于揭示被动对象状态世界模型中事件条件如何影响潜在物理结构的编码与预测功能。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a controlled diagnostic protocol to reveal how event conditioning shapes latent physical structure encoding and prediction functionality in passive object-state world models.
